hypothesis: The prior persistent-team candidate was valid and measured at 0.241645 seconds versus the valid serial baseline at 0.464905 seconds, but it did not isolate team lifetime. This contrasting implementation creates a team for each timestep, with static work over disjoint z/y rows and an implicit completion barrier before the next step. If repeated team creation is costly, it should be slower than the persistent-team version; at one thread the overhead may dominate. Controller measurements at one and four threads, including initialization, are needed to test this.
notes: This is a contrasting per-step-team implementation, not a measured speedup claim. The T1 catalog currently has one distinct measured program: the persistent-team candidate. No separate one- and four-thread timing breakdown is supplied; leave correctness and native wall-time evaluation to the controller.
transformations: Create an OpenMP parallel-for team inside each stencil timestep, requesting no more than the supplied positive thread budget.
Distribute disjoint z/y rows with static collapse(2), preserving contiguous x traversal.
Rely on each parallel-for's completion before the following timestep reads its input buffer; retain the existing timestep parity, initialization, bounds, and boundary behavior.
